gap: No result ChatGPT got states that once each station's measured inverter idle draw is added to a 40 W CPAP, the ranking changes: the Anker SOLIX S5000 (about 10 W idle, pv magazine) gives about 10.7 nights from 5,024 Wh, while the EcoFlow DELTA Pro Ultra gives 6.5–7.7 nights from 6,144 Wh (45–60 W idle) and the Jackery Explorer 5000 Plus gives 5.5 nights from 5,040 Wh (58 W idle). Those are about half the 13–16 nights ChatGPT and RidgeWatt printed.
standout_why: RidgeWatt (cited) computes nights as Wh × 0.85 ÷ 40 W with no idle term. It says outright that idle is not mentioned, and it ranks the DELTA Pro Ultra (16.3) and Explorer 5000 Plus (13.4) above the S5000 (13.3). powerstations.reviews (cited) applies a flat 85% × 80% and does not model inverter idle. pluginsolarcheck (cited) lists capacities and prices only, with no idle or CPAP figures. ChatGPT's second answer warns that idle draw 'may substantially shorten' runtimes but gives no idle number for any unit and does not re-rank. I could not open the EnoughWatts compare page (TLS certificate error), and I did not open BuyerSheet.
decides: The pick changes. At a CPAP's low load, idle draw is roughly as large as the CPAP's own draw on the big inverters (45–60 W on the DELTA Pro Ultra, 58 W on the 5000 Plus, against a 40 W CPAP), so the biggest battery does not give the most nights. Among single-box stations the Anker SOLIX S5000, which Dealectric lists via rakuten:ankersolix, comes out on top at about 10.7 nights at 40 W and 17.8 nights at 20 W with the humidifier off. Only the much pricier 12,288 Wh DELTA Pro Ultra X does better, at about 17.2 nights. Among stacks we list, the BLUETTI Apex 300 + 2× B300K (8,294.4 Wh) works out to about 14.7 nights, but only if its idle stays near 20 W with packs attached, which nobody has measured.

findings.label: Method used for every nights figure below
findings.value: nights = rated Wh × 0.85 ÷ ((CPAP W + measured idle W) × 8 h)
findings.source_title: Best Power Station for CPAP: Nights per Charge | RidgeWatt
findings.note: This keeps RidgeWatt's and ChatGPT's own inputs (0.85 factor, 40 W, 8 h) and adds only the idle term they leave out. RidgeWatt quote: 'Runtime is battery size times 0.85 ... divided by the draw'. Idle is not mentioned.
